concept.title: Harmonic Measure on the Berggren Tree Boundary — Random Walks and the 3-adic Cantor Set
concept.concept_description:
**Domain**: Pythagorean <-> Probability

**Hypothesis**: The boundary of the Berggren ternary tree of primitive Pythagorean triples is a 3-adic Cantor set, and a random walk on the tree (choosing among the three Berggren moves with probabilities p₁,p₂,p₃) converges to a harmonic measure on this boundary whose dimension and entropy are exactly computable. The conjecture: the harmonic measure of the random walk is a Bernoulli measure on the 3-adic boundary with entropy equal to the Shannon entropy H(p₁,p₂,p₃), and the spectral gap of the walk (the second eigenvalue of the associated Markov operator on the tree) is governed by the silver ratio log(1+√2) structure of the tree's growth.

**Test**: Formalize the boundary of the Berggren tree as the set of infinite words over the 3-letter alphabet {A,B,C}, i.e., the 3-adic Cantor set. Define the random walk with transition probabilities (p₁,p₂,p₃). Prove the harmonic measure is the product Bernoulli measure, compute its entropy and Hausdorff dimension, and compute the spectral gap of the Markov operator. Relate the return probabilities to the silver-ratio growth exponent already proven for the tree.

**Why now**: The catalog has exact metric growth (silver speed limit), the groupoid structure, and the hyperbolic embedding — but no probabilistic/ergodic theory. Random walks on the Berggren tree are a natural, untouched probabilistic counterpart to the deterministic geometry, connecting to the theory of random walks on hyperbolic groups, harmonic measure, and the geometry of Cantor-set boundaries.

**If true**: The Berggren tree becomes a fully understood example in the theory of random walks on hyperbolic trees — with exact harmonic measure, entropy, and spectral gap — a clean probabilistic companion to its deterministic geometry, with connections to the theory of free groups and their boundaries.

**If false**: The harmonic measure fails to be Bernoulli (e.g., the boundary carries a non-product measure), which would reveal hidden structure in how the three moves distribute mass, itself a novel statement.

concept.title: p-adic Berggren Dynamics — The Tree of Pythagorean Triples as a p-adic Dynamical System
concept.concept_description:
**Domain**: Pythagorean <-> NumberTheory

**Hypothesis**: The Berggren moves, acting on ℤ³ and preserving the Lorentz form a²+b²−c², define a rich p-adic dynamical system. Reducing the moves modulo p^k turns the infinite ternary tree into a finite p-adic dynamical system whose orbit structure, periodic points, and mixing behavior are governed by the spectral properties of the three generators (two unipotent, one hyperbolic with eigenvalues 3±2√2). The conjecture: the hyperbolic Berggren generator acts on the p-adic null cone with a computable orbit structure that is periodic for all p, with period dividing p²−1 (matching the known modular order), and the two unipotent generators act nilpotently, producing a p-adic fractal attractor on the boundary of the tree.

**Test**: Formalize the action of the three Berggren matrices on (ℤ/p^k)³. Prove the spectral classification carries over p-adically (unipotent vs. hyperbolic). Compute the exact orbit structure of the hyperbolic generator on the p-adic null cone: period, number of orbits, and the p-adic distance contraction. Establish whether the tree, viewed p-adically, has a well-defined boundary (a p-adic Cantor set) and characterize its Hausdorff dimension.

**Why now**: The existing catalog has fully formalized the real/hyperbolic geometry of the Berggren tree and the modular spectral classification of its generators. The p-adic side is essentially untouched — only one low-priority direction mentions the moves mod m. p-adic dynamics of Lorentz-preserving ternary trees connects to p-adic ergodic theory, p-adic hyperbolic geometry, and the theory of p-adic lattices, and is a genuinely fresh frontier.

**If true**: The Berggren tree acquires a p-adic structure theory mirroring its real one, opening connections to p-adic arithmetic dynamics, p-adic Fuchsian groups, and possibly to local-global questions about which triples appear at which p-adic depths.

**If false**: The p-adic orbit structure collapses to something trivial (e.g., all moves contract to a single fixed point), which is itself a clean statement about why the p-adic and real geometries of the tree differ.

concept.title: Higher-Dimensional Pythagorean Trees — Generalizing the Berggren Tree to Pythagorean Quadruples and Hyperspheres
concept.concept_description:
**Domain**: Pythagorean <-> Geometry

**Hypothesis**: The Berggren ternary tree of primitive Pythagorean triples is the 2-dimensional case of a general family of trees of primitive Pythagorean n-tuples (solutions of x₁²+…+xₙ² = y²). For each n ≥ 3 there is a higher-dimensional "Pythagorean tree" generated by a finite set of Lorentz-preserving integer matrices acting on the null cone of the (n+1)-dimensional Lorentz form, generalizing the three Berggren moves. The conjecture: for n = 3 (Pythagorean quadruples / hyperspheres) there is a finite generating set of integer matrices, the tree has a well-defined hyperbolic embedding in the (n+1)-dimensional Poincaré ball, and its metric growth exponent is an exactly computable algebraic number generalizing the silver ratio log(1+√2).

**Test**: Formalize the null cone of the (n+1)-dimensional Lorentz form and the group of its integral Lorentz-preserving automorphisms. For n = 3, exhibit a finite generating set of matrices producing a tree of primitive Pythagorean quadruples, prove the tree's branching structure (how many children per node), and compute the hyperbolic metric growth exponent. Generalize the Berggren groupoid, the star-line structure, and the totient law to the higher-dimensional setting.

**Why now**: The entire existing corpus is the 2-dimensional Berggren tree. Higher-dimensional Pythagorean trees (quadruples, quintuples, hyperspheres) are a natural, essentially unexplored generalization that would extend the groupoid, hyperbolic-geometry, and growth machinery to a whole family of objects — and hypersphere packing / kissing-number questions give it concrete applications.

**If true**: A full higher-dimensional theory of Pythagorean trees emerges — groupoid, hyperbolic embedding, silver-ratio-type growth — generalizing the Berggren tree and connecting to sphere packing, quadratic forms in higher dimensions, and the arithmetic of the higher Lorentz groups.

**If false**: The higher-dimensional tree fails to be a clean ternary tree (e.g., branching grows with n, or the growth exponent is not algebraic), which itself characterizes how the beautiful 2-dimensional structure fails to generalize.

# The descent complex of a Pythagorean `n`-tuple

The catalog develops the Berggren tree (`n = 2`) and its quadruple analogue (`n = 3`)
through *reflection moves* of the integral Lorentz group of `x₁² + … + xₙ² = y²`:
for a sign pattern `ε ∈ {±1}ⁿ` the move sends the height `y` to `2y − ε·x`, so it
*descends* exactly when `ε · x > y`.

A sign pattern is the same thing as the set `S ⊆ {1,…,n}` of its minus signs, so the
collection of descending patterns at a node is a family of subsets: the **descent complex**
of the node.  This file develops that complex for *arbitrary* `n`; it is the structure
governing how many parents a node of the `n`-dimensional Pythagorean graph has.

Main results.

* `signedSum_eq_total_sub` : the sign-pattern sum is `∑ xᵢ − 2 ∑_{i∈S} xᵢ`.
* `DescendsOn.mono` : the descent complex is **downward closed** (an abstract simplicial
  complex on the coordinate set).
* `DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl` : every face `S` satisfies `#Sᶜ ≥ 2`, i.e. `#S ≤ n − 2`.
  This dimension bound is forced by the Pythagorean relation.
* `DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl_union` : the same bound holds for the union of two
  **disjoint** faces — a genuine strengthening.
* `descent_singleton_unique_of_three` : for `n = 3` at most one singleton is a face, which
  re-derives the catalog's `descend_minus_index_unique` from the general theory.

namespace HigherPythagoreanDescent

open Finset

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A Pythagorean `n`-tuple: an integral point `x` of the null cone with height `d`. -/
def IsPythTuple (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) : Prop := ∑ i, x i ^ 2 = d ^ 2

/-- The signed coordinate sum `ε · x`, where the sign pattern `ε` is `-1` exactly on `S`. -/
def signedSum (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) : ℤ := ∑ i, (if i ∈ S then -x i else x i)

/-- The sign pattern with minus signs on `S` *descends* at the node `(x, d)` when the
reflection move `d ↦ 2d − ε·x` strictly lowers the height. -/
def DescendsOn (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) : Prop := d < signedSum S x

lemma descendsOn_iff_height_lt (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) :
    DescendsOn S x d ↔ 2 * d - signedSum S x < d := by
  unfold DescendsOn; constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- `ε · x = ∑ xᵢ − 2 ∑_{i ∈ S} xᵢ`. -/
lemma signedSum_eq_total_sub (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) :
    signedSum S x = (∑ i, x i) - 2 * ∑ i ∈ S, x i := by
  have hpt : ∀ i : Fin n, (if i ∈ S then -x i else x i)
      = x i - (if i ∈ S then 2 * x i else 0) := by
    intro i
    by_cases h : i ∈ S <;> simp [h, two_mul]
  calc signedSum S x = ∑ i, (x i - (if i ∈ S then 2 * x i else 0)) := by
        unfold signedSum; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hpt i
    _ = (∑ i, x i) - ∑ i, (if i ∈ S then 2 * x i else 0) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    _ = (∑ i, x i) - 2 * ∑ i ∈ S, x i := by
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_mem, Finset.univ_inter, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The empty sign pattern is the all-plus move. -/
lemma signedSum_empty (x : Fin n → ℤ) : signedSum (∅ : Finset (Fin n)) x = ∑ i, x i := by
  simp [signedSum]

/-! ## The dimension bound: a face has at least two coordinates outside it -/

/-- Each coordinate of a Pythagorean tuple is bounded by the height. -/
lemma coord_le_height {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) (j : Fin n) : x j ≤ d := by
  have hsq : x j ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 2 := by
    rw [← h]
    exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun i => x i ^ 2) (fun i _ => sq_nonneg (x i))
      (Finset.mem_univ j)
  nlinarith

/-- A set of coordinates whose sum exceeds the height must contain at least two indices.
This is the engine of the whole dimension bound. -/
lemma two_le_card_of_sum_gt {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) {T : Finset (Fin n)} (hT : d < ∑ i ∈ T, x i) : 2 ≤ T.card := by
  by_contra hcard
  push_neg at hcard
  interval_cases hc : T.card
  · rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at hc
    subst hc
    simp at hT
    omega
  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp hc
    rw [Finset.sum_singleton] at hT
    exact absurd (coord_le_height hd h j) (by omega)

/-- **Dimension bound.**  Every face of the descent complex has at least two coordinates in
its complement: `#S ≤ n − 2`.  In particular a descending sign pattern always has at least
two plus signs. -/
theorem DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hS : DescendsOn S x d) : 2 ≤ Sᶜ.card := by
  refine two_le_card_of_sum_gt hd h (T := Sᶜ) ?_
  have hsum : ∑ i ∈ S, x i + ∑ i ∈ Sᶜ, x i = ∑ i, x i := Finset.sum_add_sum_compl S x
  have hnn : 0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ S, x i := Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hx i
  have := hS
  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at this
  linarith

theorem DescendsOn.card_le {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hS : DescendsOn S x d) : S.card + 2 ≤ n := by
  have hc := hS.two_le_card_compl hx hd h
  have : S.card + Sᶜ.card = n := by
    rw [Finset.card_add_card_compl]
    simp
  omega

theorem DescendsOn.mono {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) {S T : Finset (Fin n)}
    (hST : S ⊆ T) (hT : DescendsOn T x d) : DescendsOn S x d := by
  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at hT ⊢
  have : ∑ i ∈ S, x i ≤ ∑ i ∈ T, x i :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hST fun i _ _ => hx i
  linarith

  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at hS hT
  have hunion : ∑ i ∈ S ∪ T, x i = ∑ i ∈ S, x i + ∑ i ∈ T, x i :=
    Finset.sum_union hdisj
  have hsplit : ∑ i ∈ S ∪ T, x i + ∑ i ∈ (S ∪ T)ᶜ, x i = ∑ i, x i :=
    Finset.sum_add_sum_compl (S ∪ T) x

through *reflection moves* of the integral Lorentz group of `x₁² + … + xₙ² = y²`:

governing how many parents a node of the `n`-dimensional Pythagorean graph has.

* `signedSum_eq_total_sub` : the sign-pattern sum is `∑ xᵢ − 2 ∑_{i∈S} xᵢ`.

* `DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl` : every face `S` satisfies `#Sᶜ ≥ 2`, i.e. `#S ≤ n − 2`.

* `DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl_union` : the same bound holds for the union of two

/-- A Pythagorean `n`-tuple: an integral point `x` of the null cone with height `d`. -/
def IsPythTuple (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) : Prop := ∑ i, x i ^ 2 = d ^ 2

/-- The signed coordinate sum `ε · x`, where the sign pattern `ε` is `-1` exactly on `S`. -/
def signedSum (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) : ℤ := ∑ i, (if i ∈ S then -x i else x i)

/-- The sign pattern with minus signs on `S` *descends* at the node `(x, d)` when the
reflection move `d ↦ 2d − ε·x` strictly lowers the height. -/
def DescendsOn (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) : Prop := d < signedSum S x

lemma descendsOn_iff_height_lt (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (d : ℤ) :
    DescendsOn S x d ↔ 2 * d - signedSum S x < d := by
  unfold DescendsOn; constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- `ε · x = ∑ xᵢ − 2 ∑_{i ∈ S} xᵢ`. -/
lemma signedSum_eq_total_sub (S : Finset (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℤ) :
    signedSum S x = (∑ i, x i) - 2 * ∑ i ∈ S, x i := by
  have hpt : ∀ i : Fin n, (if i ∈ S then -x i else x i)

    intro i

  calc signedSum S x = ∑ i, (x i - (if i ∈ S then 2 * x i else 0)) := by
        unfold signedSum; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => hpt i
    _ = (∑ i, x i) - ∑ i, (if i ∈ S then 2 * x i else 0) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    _ = (∑ i, x i) - 2 * ∑ i ∈ S, x i := by
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_mem, Finset.univ_inter, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The empty sign pattern is the all-plus move. -/
lemma signedSum_empty (x : Fin n → ℤ) : signedSum (∅ : Finset (Fin n)) x = ∑ i, x i := by
  simp [signedSum]

/-- Each coordinate of a Pythagorean tuple is bounded by the height. -/
lemma coord_le_height {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)

  have hsq : x j ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 2 := by
    rw [← h]

This is the engine of the whole dimension bound. -/
lemma two_le_card_of_sum_gt {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)

  by_contra hcard
  push_neg at hcard
  interval_cases hc : T.card
  · rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at hc
    subst hc
    simp at hT
    omega
  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp hc
    rw [Finset.sum_singleton] at hT
    exact absurd (coord_le_height hd h j) (by omega)

two plus signs. -/
theorem DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hS : DescendsOn S x d) : 2 ≤ Sᶜ.card := by
  refine two_le_card_of_sum_gt hd h (T := Sᶜ) ?_
  have hsum : ∑ i ∈ S, x i + ∑ i ∈ Sᶜ, x i = ∑ i, x i := Finset.sum_add_sum_compl S x
  have hnn : 0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ S, x i := Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hx i
  have := hS
  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at this
  linarith

/-- The cardinality form of the dimension bound. -/
theorem DescendsOn.card_le {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : IsPythTuple x d) {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hS : DescendsOn S x d) : S.card + 2 ≤ n := by
  have hc := hS.two_le_card_compl hx hd h
  have : S.card + Sᶜ.card = n := by
    rw [Finset.card_add_card_compl]
    simp
  omega

/-- **The descent complex is downward closed**: if a sign pattern with minus signs on `T`
descends, so does every pattern with fewer minus signs. -/
theorem DescendsOn.mono {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) {S T : Finset (Fin n)}
    (hST : S ⊆ T) (hT : DescendsOn T x d) : DescendsOn S x d := by
  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at hT ⊢
  have : ∑ i ∈ S, x i ≤ ∑ i ∈ T, x i :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hST fun i _ _ => hx i
  linarith

/-- **Disjoint faces still obey the dimension bound on their union.**  If two disjoint sign
patterns both descend then their union already has two coordinates outside it. -/
theorem DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl_union {x : Fin n → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d) (h : IsPythTuple x d) {S T : Finset (Fin n)} (hdisj : Disjoint S T)
    (hS : DescendsOn S x d) (hT : DescendsOn T x d) : 2 ≤ (S ∪ T)ᶜ.card := by
  refine two_le_card_of_sum_gt hd h (T := (S ∪ T)ᶜ) ?_
  rw [DescendsOn, signedSum_eq_total_sub] at hS hT
  have hunion : ∑ i ∈ S ∪ T, x i = ∑ i ∈ S, x i + ∑ i ∈ T, x i :=
    Finset.sum_union hdisj
  have hsplit : ∑ i ∈ S ∪ T, x i + ∑ i ∈ (S ∪ T)ᶜ, x i = ∑ i, x i :=
    Finset.sum_add_sum_compl (S ∪ T) x
  linarith

/-! ## Dimension three: at most one singleton face -/

/-- **Uniqueness of the one-minus descent in dimension three.**  For a Pythagorean triple of
space coordinates (i.e. a Pythagorean quadruple) at most one single sign flip descends. -/
theorem descent_singleton_unique_of_three {x : Fin 3 → ℤ} {d : ℤ} (hd : 0 ≤ d) (h : IsPythTuple x d) {i j : Fin 3}
    (hi : DescendsOn {i} x d) (hj : DescendsOn {j} x d) : i = j := by
  by_contra hij
  have hdisj : Disjoint ({i} : Finset (Fin 3)) {j} := by
    simp [hij]
  have hcard := DescendsOn.two_le_card_compl_union hd h hdisj hi hj
  have hu : ({i} ∪ {j} : Finset (Fin 3)).card = 2 := by
    rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj]
    simp
  have hsum : ({i} ∪ {j} : Finset (Fin 3)).card + (({i} ∪ {j} : Finset (Fin 3))ᶜ).card = 3 := by
    rw [Finset.card_add_card_compl]
    simp
  omega

/-! ## Bridge to the catalog's quadruple machinery (`n = 3`) -/

/-- The `n = 3` null cone is exactly the catalog's `IsPythQuadruple`. -/
theorem isPythTuple_iff_isPythQuadruple (a b c d : ℤ) :
    IsPythTuple ![a, b, c] d ↔ IsPythQuadruple a b c d := by
  unfold IsPythTuple IsPythQuadruple
  simp [Fin.sum_univ_three]

theorem descendsOn_empty_iff_catalog (a b c d : ℤ) :
    DescendsOn (∅ : Finset (Fin 3)) ![a, b, c] d ↔ HigherPythagorean.Descends 1 1 1 a b c d := by
  unfold DescendsOn HigherPythagorean.Descends
  rw [signedSum_empty]
  simp [Fin.sum_univ_three]

  unfold DescendsOn HigherPythagorean.Descends signedSum
  simp [Fin.sum_univ_three]

      simp only [pell, pellStep]
      constructor <;> omega

  | succ k ih =>

      simp only [pell, pellStep]
      push_cast
      omega

  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := pell_pos n
  simp only [pell, pellStep]
  omega

theorem quintuple_isPythTuple {t d : ℤ} (h : d ^ 2 = 2 * t ^ 2 + 2) :

  unfold IsPythTuple quintuple
  simp [Fin.sum_univ_four]
  linarith

  unfold DescendsOn signedSum quintuple
  simp [Fin.sum_univ_four]
  linarith

theorem two_face_card : ({0, 1} : Finset (Fin 4)).card = 2 := by decide

theorem quintuple_primitive {t : ℤ} (g : ℤ) (hg : ∀ i, g ∣ quintuple t i) : IsUnit g := by

    ∃ (x : Fin 4 → ℤ) (d : ℤ) (S : Finset (Fin 4)),

    refine ⟨(N + 1).toNat, ?_⟩
    have := Int.self_le_toNat (N + 1)
    omega
  set t := (pell (n + 1)).1 with hts
  set d := (pell (n + 1)).2 with hds
  have hnorm : d ^ 2 = 2 * t ^ 2 + 2 := pell_norm (n + 1)
  have ht7 : 7 ≤ t := pell_fst_ge_seven n
  have hdN : N < d := by
    have h1 : ((n : ℤ) + 1) + 2 ≤ d := by
      have := pell_snd_ge (n + 1)
      push_cast at this
      linarith
    linarith
  have hdpos : 0 < d := by linarith [(pell_pos (n + 1)).2]
  refine ⟨quintuple t, d, {0, 1}, quintuple_isPythTuple hnorm,
    quintuple_nonneg (by linarith), hdN, ?_, two_face_card, ?_⟩
  · intro g hg
    exact quintuple_primitive (t := t) g hg
  · exact quintuple_two_face (by linarith) hdpos hnorm

/-!
# The finite generating set of dimension three: eight signed reflections

The catalog contains the single reflection matrix `HigherPythagorean.quadRefl` of the Lorentz
form of signature `(3,1)`.  The dimension-two Berggren tree, however, is generated by *three*
matrices, obtained from one reflection by conjugating with the diagonal sign matrices.  This
file constructs the dimension-three analogue: the **eight signed reflections**

`Rε = Sε · quadRefl · Sε`,  `Sε = diag(ε₁, ε₂, ε₃, 1)`,  `ε ∈ {±1}³`,

and proves that they are exactly the moves whose combinatorics is analysed in
`Catalog.Physics.HigherPythagoreanTrees.ExactBranching`.

Main results.

* `signMat_isIntegralLorentz`, `signedRefl_isIntegralLorentz` : the eight matrices are integral
  automorphisms of the Lorentz form, hence act on the null cone of Pythagorean quadruples.
* `signedRefl_mulVec` : the explicit action `(x, d) ↦ (xᵢ − εᵢk, d − k)` with `k = ε·x − d`.
* `signedRefl_height` : the height transforms by `d ↦ 2d − ε·x`, which is precisely the
  quantity governing `HigherPythagorean.Descends`.
* `signedRefl_involutive` : each generator is an involution, so the moves generate a quotient
  of a free product of copies of `ℤ/2`.
* `descends_iff_signedRefl_height_lt` : the bridge between the matrix group and the branching
  analysis; `signedRefl_preserves_content` : primitivity is preserved.
-/

namespace HigherPythagoreanSigned

open Matrix HigherPythagorean

/-- The diagonal sign matrix `diag(ε₁, ε₂, ε₃, 1)`. -/
def signMat (e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ) : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℤ :=
  !![e₁, 0, 0, 0; 0, e₂, 0, 0; 0, 0, e₃, 0; 0, 0, 0, 1]

/-- The signed reflection `Rε = Sε · R · Sε`. -/
def signedRefl (e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ) : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℤ :=
  signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * quadRefl * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃

/-- Sign matrices are integral Lorentz automorphisms. -/
theorem signMat_isIntegralLorentz {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂)
    (h₃ : IsSign e₃) : IsIntegralLorentz (signMat e₁ e₂ e₃) := by
  have s₁ : e₁ * e₁ = 1 := by rcases h₁ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  have s₂ : e₂ * e₂ = 1 := by rcases h₂ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  have s₃ : e₃ * e₃ = 1 := by rcases h₃ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  unfold IsIntegralLorentz
  rw [lorentzJ_three]
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
    simp [signMat, Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_four, s₁, s₂, s₃]

/-- **The eight generators are integral Lorentz automorphisms.** -/
theorem signedRefl_isIntegralLorentz {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂)
    (h₃ : IsSign e₃) : IsIntegralLorentz (signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃) :=
  ((signMat_isIntegralLorentz h₁ h₂ h₃).mul quadRefl_isIntegralLorentz).mul
    (signMat_isIntegralLorentz h₁ h₂ h₃)

/-- The signed Berggren shift `k = ε·x − d`. -/
def sk (e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d : ℤ) : ℤ := e₁ * a + e₂ * b + e₃ * c - d

/-- **Explicit action of a generator** on a quadruple. -/
theorem signedRefl_mulVec {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂) (h₃ : IsSign e₃)
    (a b c d : ℤ) :
    signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃ *ᵥ ![a, b, c, d] =
      ![a - e₁ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d, b - e₂ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d,
        c - e₃ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d, d - sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d] := by
  rcases h₁ with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h₂ with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h₃ with rfl | rfl <;>
    (ext i
     fin_cases i <;>
       simp [signedRefl, signMat, quadRefl, sk, Matrix.mulVec, Matrix.mul_apply, dotProduct,
         Fin.sum_univ_four] <;> ring)

/-- **The height law**: a generator sends the height `d` to `2d − ε·x`. -/
theorem signedRefl_height {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂) (h₃ : IsSign e₃)
    (a b c d : ℤ) :
    (signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃ *ᵥ ![a, b, c, d]) 3 = 2 * d - (e₁ * a + e₂ * b + e₃ * c) := by
  rw [signedRefl_mulVec h₁ h₂ h₃]
  simp [sk]
  ring

/-- **Bridge to the branching analysis.**  The sign pattern `ε` descends at `(a,b,c,d)` in the
sense of the catalog exactly when the matrix `Rε` lowers the height. -/
theorem descends_iff_signedRefl_height_lt {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂)
    (h₃ : IsSign e₃) (a b c d : ℤ) :
    Descends e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d ↔ (signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃ *ᵥ ![a, b, c, d]) 3 < d := by
  rw [signedRefl_height h₁ h₂ h₃]
  unfold Descends
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- Sign matrices are involutions. -/
theorem signMat_mul_self {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂) (h₃ : IsSign e₃) :
    signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ = 1 := by
  have s₁ : e₁ * e₁ = 1 := by rcases h₁ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  have s₂ : e₂ * e₂ = 1 := by rcases h₂ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  have s₃ : e₃ * e₃ = 1 := by rcases h₃ with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
    simp [signMat, Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_four, s₁, s₂, s₃]

/-- Each generator is an involution, so the eight moves generate a quotient of a free product
of copies of `ℤ/2`. -/
theorem signedRefl_involutive {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂) (h₃ : IsSign e₃) :
    signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃ * signedRefl e₁ e₂ e₃ = 1 := by
  have hS := signMat_mul_self h₁ h₂ h₃
  have hR := quadRefl_mul_self
  unfold signedRefl
  calc signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * quadRefl * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ *
        (signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * quadRefl * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃)
      = signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * quadRefl * (signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃) * quadRefl *
        signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ := by noncomm_ring
    _ = signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * (quadRefl * quadRefl) * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ := by
        rw [hS]; noncomm_ring
    _ = signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ * signMat e₁ e₂ e₃ := by rw [hR]; noncomm_ring
    _ = 1 := hS

/-- The generators preserve the Pythagorean quadruple relation. -/
theorem signedRefl_pyth {e₁ e₂ e₃ : ℤ} (h₁ : IsSign e₁) (h₂ : IsSign e₂) (h₃ : IsSign e₃)
    {a b c d : ℤ} (h : IsPythQuadruple a b c d) :
    IsPythQuadruple (a - e₁ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) (b - e₂ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d)
      (c - e₃ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) (d - sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) := by
  unfold IsPythQuadruple sk at *
  rcases h₁ with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h₂ with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h₃ with rfl | rfl <;>
    linear_combination h

/-- The generators preserve the content, hence primitivity. -/
theorem signedRefl_preserves_content (e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d : ℤ) :
    content a b c d ∣ content (a - e₁ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) (b - e₂ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d)
      (c - e₃ * sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) (d - sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d) := by
  have hx := content_dvd_fst a b c d
  have hy := content_dvd_snd a b c d
  have hz := content_dvd_thd a b c d
  have hw := content_dvd_fth a b c d
  have hk : (content a b c d : ℤ) ∣ sk e₁ e₂ e₃ a b c d := by
    unfold sk
    exact dvd_sub (dvd_add (dvd_add (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hx _) (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hy _))
      (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hz _)) hw
  exact dvd_content (dvd_sub hx (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hk _)) (dvd_sub hy (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hk _))
    (dvd_sub hz (Dvd.dvd.mul_left hk _)) (dvd_sub hw hk)

/-- The all-plus generator is the catalog's reflection matrix. -/
theorem signedRefl_one : signedRefl 1 1 1 = quadRefl := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
    simp [signedRefl, signMat, quadRefl, Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_four]

end HigherPythagoreanSigned

# Computational evidence — higher-dimensional Pythagorean trees

All numbers below were produced by exhaustive enumeration before the Lean formalisation, and
every qualitative statement they suggested is now a machine-checked theorem in
`Catalog/Physics/HigherPythagoreanTrees/`.  The tables themselves are exploratory (they were
produced by a scratch enumeration, not by a Lean proof) and are recorded only as motivation.

## 1. Branching of the quadruple graph (`n = 3`)

Reflection moves are indexed by sign patterns `ε ∈ {±1}³`; the move sends the height `d` to
`2d − ε·x`, so it *descends* iff `ε·x > d`, is *neutral* iff `ε·x = d`, and is a *child*
otherwise.

Enumerating all 135 primitive quadruples `(a,b,c,d)` with `0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ c`, `d ≤ 60`:

| # descending patterns | # nodes |
|---|---|
| 0 | 1  (only `(0,0,1,1)`) |
| 1 | 48 |
| 2 | 86 |
| ≥ 3 | 0 |

Never more than two descents — matching the catalog bound and our exact count.  Examples with
two descents: `(0,3,4,5)`, `(1,4,8,9)`, `(2,6,9,11)`, `(0,5,12,13)`.

Counting *children* (strictly ascending patterns) for nodes with all coordinates positive gave
only the values **6 and 7**, never 5 or 8.  Formalised as
`HigherPythagoreanBranching.quad_children_card`: the count is `6` iff the weak harmonic defect
`a(b+c) ≤ bc ∨ b(a+c) ≤ ac ∨ c(a+b) ≤ ab` holds, and `7` otherwise.

Seven-children nodes found: `(4,4,7,9)`, `(6,6,7,11)`, `(8,9,12,17)`, `(6,6,17,19)`,
`(8,11,16,21)`, `(9,12,20,25)`, … .  The sub-pattern `(2m, 2m, 2m²−1, 2m²+1)` (`m = 2, 3, …`)
reproduces `(4,4,7,9)`, `(6,6,17,19)`, `(8,8,31,33)`, and is the family formalised in
`quad_children_seven_family`.  The catalog family `(1, 2m, 2m², 2m²+1)` supplies the
six-children case.

## 2. Two-element descent faces in dimension four

For `n = 3` no pair of coordinates can be flipped simultaneously and still descend.  Searching
primitive quintuples `(x₁,x₂,x₃,x₄; d)` with `d ≤ 60` produced many two-element descents, the
first ones with all coordinates positive being

`(1,1,7,7; 10)`, `(1,2,8,10; 13)`, `(1,1,5,13; 14)`, … .

The family `(1,1,t,t; d)` with `d² = 2t² + 2` is Pell: `(t,d) = (1,2), (7,10), (41,58),
(239,338), …`, generated by `(t,d) ↦ (3t+2d, 4t+3d)`.  Formalised in
`HigherPythagoreanPell.dim_four_descent_bound_sharp`, which shows the general bound
`#S ≤ n − 2` is attained for `n = 4`.

## 3. Mirror (neutral) nodes and the divisor law

Neutral moves exist only from dimension three on.  Enumeration of neutral nodes sorted by
smallest coordinate `a` gave

| `a` | neutral nodes `(a, b, c, d)` | count | `τ(a²)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `(1,2,2,3)` | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | `(2,3,6,7)`, `(2,4,4,6)`, `(2,6,3,7)` | 3 | 3 |
| 3 | `(3,4,12,13)`, `(3,6,6,9)`, `(3,12,4,13)` | 3 | 3 |
| 4 | 5 nodes | 5 | 5 |
| 6 | 9 nodes | 9 | 9 |

The counts are exactly `τ(a²)`, the number of divisors of `a²` — the observation formalised as
`HigherPythagoreanDivisor.mirror_pairs_card`, via the bijection `a² = p·q ↦ (a, a+p, a+q,
a+p+q)`.

## 4. Growth constants

`ρₙ = (√n+1)/(√n−1)`: `ρ₂ = 3+2√2 ≈ 5.8284`, `ρ₃ = 2+√3 ≈ 3.7321`, `ρ₄ = 3`, `ρ₉ = 2`,
`ρₙ → 1`.  Critical exponents `δ = log(branching)/log ρ`:

| dimension | branching | `ρ` | `δ` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 | 5.8284 | 0.6233 |
| 3 | 6 | 3.7321 | 1.3603 |
| 3 | 7 | 3.7321 | 1.4771 |

The strict separation `δ₂ < 1 < δ₃` is proved in
`HigherPythagoreanGrowth.criticalExponent_three_gt_two`.

# Future directions — higher-dimensional Pythagorean trees

The results proved in this cycle (`Catalog/Physics/HigherPythagoreanTrees/`) settle the
qualitative shape of the generalisation:

* the descent complex of a Pythagorean `n`-tuple is a downward-closed family with all faces of
  size `≤ n − 2` (`DescendsOn.card_le`), sharp for `n = 3` (only singletons) and for `n = 4`
  (infinitely many two-element faces, `dim_four_descent_bound_sharp`);
* in dimension three the branching number is exactly `6` or `7`, decided by a weak harmonic
  (Egyptian-fraction) inequality (`quad_children_card`) — so the graph is **not** a regular
  tree, and both values occur infinitely often;
* the universal lower bound `n + 1` for the branching (`card_children_ge`) is attained exactly
  in the Berggren case `n = 2`;
* the sharp metric growth constant `ρₙ = (√n+1)/(√n−1)` is a quadratic unit, `ρ₃ = 2+√3` is the
  fundamental unit of `ℤ[√3]`, and the critical exponent jumps across `1` from dimension two to
  dimension three (`criticalExponent_three_gt_two`);
* mirror (height-neutral) nodes are exactly the fixed points of the generators, and they obey a
  **divisor law**: `τ(a²)` of them sit above each first coordinate `a`
  (`mirror_pairs_card`).

The following conjectures are the natural next targets.

## Conjecture A (sharpness of the face bound in every dimension)

**Statement.** For every `n ≥ 3` there exist infinitely many primitive Pythagorean `n`-tuples
whose descent complex contains a face of size exactly `n − 2`.

*The key insight is* that a face of size `n − 2` is a solution of a generalised Pell system:
taking the two "large" coordinates equal to `t` and the `n − 2` small ones equal to `1` reduces

concept.title: Markoff Tree Transfer — Carrying the Berggren Tree's Machinery to the Markoff Tree
concept.concept_description:
**Domain**: Pythagorean <-> Algebra

**Hypothesis**: The Berggren ternary tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and the Markoff tree are isomorphic as Lorentz-preserving ternary trees. The Berggren moves generate a groupoid acting on the null cone of the Lorentz form a²+b²−c²; the Markoff tree is generated by Vieta involutions preserving the Markoff form x²+y²+z²−3xyz. Both are ternary, both embed in hyperbolic space, and both have a "silver-ratio" growth spine (Berggren) / a golden-ratio spine (Markoff). The conjecture: there is a birational (or integer) transfer map carrying the Berggren tree's proven machinery — the groupoid structure, the hyperbolic embedding, the silver-ratio metric growth, the totient law for star arms — onto the Markoff tree.

**Test**: Formalize the Markoff tree as a ternary tree of integer triples under Vieta involutions. Construct the explicit transfer map from Berggren triples to Markoff triples (via the known parametrization of Markoff triples by Christoffel words / the Stern-Brocot tree, which is itself the Berggren tree in disguise). Prove the map is a tree isomorphism preserving the ternary branching, and transfer at least one structural theorem (e.g., the uniqueness of the growth spine, or the groupoid action) from the Berggren side to the Markoff side.

**Why now**: The Markoff uniqueness conjecture (that every Markoff triple is uniquely determined by its largest element) is a famous open problem. The Berggren tree already carries a fully formalized groupoid, hyperbolic geometry, and exact growth theory in this catalog. A transfer theorem would be a genuinely new bridge from a solved structure to an open one — the highest-value possible outcome.

**If true**: The Berggren tree's machinery becomes a tool for the Markoff tree, opening a new attack line on Markoff uniqueness and the geometric structure of Markoff triples (which connect to the modular group, continued fractions, and the theory of quadratic forms).

**If false**: The failure point (where the transfer breaks — e.g., the Lorentz form vs. Markoff form are not conjugate over ℤ) is itself a theorem about why the two trees differ, clarifying the boundary between them.
